details.description: Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 is a mixture-of-experts chat model from Alibaba's Qwen team, with 235 billion total parameters and 22 billion activated per token. Released July 21, 2025 as an update to the original Qwen3-235B-A22B, it targets instruction following, logical reasoning, mathematics, science, coding, and tool use. Qwen's own model card states it runs in non-thinking mode only (no <think> reasoning blocks), unlike its sibling Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507. It is offered on Amazon Bedrock as 'Qwen3 235B A22B 2507' (model ID qwen.qwen3-235b-a22b-2507-v1:0), listed there as an Active model with a 262,144-token context window.
advantages: Scores 83.0 on MMLU-Pro, a knowledge and reasoning benchmark (Qwen's model card).
Scores 70.3 on AIME25, a competition math benchmark (Qwen's model card).
Scores 51.8 on LiveCodeBench v6, a coding benchmark (Qwen's model card).
Scores 79.2 on Arena-Hard v2, an instruction-following comparison benchmark (Qwen's model card).
Scores 70.9 on BFCL-v3, a tool/function-calling benchmark (Qwen's model card).
Supports tool calling and agent workflows through the Qwen-Agent framework, including MCP configuration.
disadvantages: Non-thinking mode only; Qwen's card states it does not generate <think></think> reasoning blocks, unlike the sibling Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 checkpoint.
use_cases: General-purpose instruction following and multi-turn chat
Code generation and software engineering tasks
Agentic tool calling and MCP-based agent workflows
Long-document processing up to Qwen's stated 262,144-token native context

sources.title: Qwen — Qwen3 235B A22B 2507 - Amazon Bedrock User Guide

notes: AWS Bedrock's model card lists a launch date of April 28, 2025, which is the original base Qwen3-235B-A22B family's release date (per Qwen's blog and GitHub repo); this specific Instruct-2507 checkpoint was released July 21, 2025 per the QwenLM/Qwen3 GitHub repo's changelog (Thinking-2507 followed July 25, 2025). Catalog's max_output_tokens (131,072) matches neither source: Qwen's card recommends 16,384 output tokens for most queries, and Amazon Bedrock's current model card caps this endpoint at 8K max output tokens; catalog value kept per instructions. Bedrock's card also flags 'Reasoning: Supported' for this model, which conflicts with Qwen's card stating the Instruct-2507 checkpoint is non-thinking only — likely a generic Bedrock feature flag rather than evidence of actual <think> support, so not claimed above. Identified as the Instruct-2507 (not Thinking-2507) checkpoint because AWS's EULA link for this exact model ID points to Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507's license page.
